relevant_symbols.conclusion: The netlink policy types transport attributes. Segment index and count each occupy four bits. This is not a read-only opcode allowlist.
Response accumulation is limited to 2048 bytes. The receiver reads current_seq but does not compare it with expected_seq; it does not validate msgref or the advertised total length here.
Events are consumed only while utf_monitor is enabled. Known UTF event IDs are routed through the segmented or unsegmented branch.

The loader tries API2 utf-2.bin, with bus suffixes for USB and SDIO, then falls back to utf.bin. API1 forces the 10.1 WMI and HTT operation versions. Normal board data and, when necessary, the normal firmware OTP image are reused.

Start requires the OFF state. It rejects an already running UTF instance with EALREADY and an active driver with EBUSY. It powers hardware, starts the core in UTF mode and changes driver state; it does not stop an active WLAN automatically.
Stop shuts down the core and HIF power, frees UTF resources and returns the driver to OFF. It does not restore or start normal WLAN firmware.
The raw WMI command requires UTF state, DATA and WMI_CMDID. It copies an opaque payload and transmits the supplied command ID without validating command safety or target semantics.
The TLV path splits data into 252-byte pieces, adds a TLV and little-endian segment header, and sends the literal WMI_PDEV_UTF_CMDID. Exact target compatibility is not established.
Command zero without DATA queries the host testmode ABI. The same command with DATA transmits segmented TLV data. Unknown commands return EOPNOTSUPP.

relevant_symbols.conclusion: The boot session is controlled by done_sent. DONE sets the flag before the exchange; this function does not clear it automatically on an exchange error.
READ_MEMORY uses chunks no larger than 256 bytes. It returns EBUSY after DONE and propagates HIF exchange errors. It is neither a runtime WMI memory API nor an address allowlist.
Register reads and writes use distinct opcodes and the same boot-phase gate. The existence of a read operation does not prove that arbitrary register reads lack side effects.
Memory writes and target code execution are separate primitives. Neither was executed here; neither belongs to a read-only allowlist.
Compressed download and start-address operations mutate target state. Their existence does not establish safe or authorized execution.

relevant_symbols.conclusion: The reader uses target-to-host Copy Engine DMA in bounded chunks. A mutex serializes access; completion timeouts, sizes and buffer addresses are checked. A read still programs CE/DMA state.
Section and destination-size checks limit copying. Gaps are marked as not copied and read errors stop the loop. The QCA988X table itself uses whole register regions without section tables.

The generic reader copies selected regions. Destination size is checked and failures can produce zero-length sections. Other chip layouts may require an IRAM configuration write; the QCA988X table shown here contains no IRAM region.
Crash work collects registers, Copy Engine state and memory, then starts recovery. Deliberately crashing firmware is not a passive read and was not performed.
The BMI exchange allocates request/response DMA buffers, propagates errors and bounds received length by requested length.
Completion is polled until the BMI communication deadline; expiration returns ETIMEDOUT.

audited_claims.conclusion: RX contract defines32-bit TSF and WLAN/BT timestamps plus8-bit fractional-location timestamp. WLAN/BT is described at1us resolution, without beacon updates; fractional clock80MHz/12.5ns is an example.
limits: WLAN/BT timestamp is not demonstrated UTC/wall-clock time. Actual device clock frequency, rollover/offset calibration and export are unmeasured.

audited_claims.conclusion: series_bw documents4-bit rate with2-bit preamble selector: OFDM,CCK,HT,VHT; VHT encoding is legal0..9 through256-QAM. Descriptor also exposes NSS,LDPC,STBC,SGI and TXBF.
limits: Negative scope is this normal descriptor contract only; it does not prove absence of deeper mapper/FEC/pilot tables or all undocumented baseband features.
References to160MHz/four-stream illegal combinations are generic schema text, not AR9888 board capability proof.

limits: ABI is SHARED_ONLY, not proof of exact AR9888 implementation or successful raw ADC capture. Signedness, analog sampling stage, units and complex encoding are not resolved by uint16 arrays.

audited_claims.conclusion: No concrete AR9888 ADCCAPTURE callback registration was found in the reviewed target startup/dispatch/TCMD files. Shared generated wrapper initializes callbackNULL, calls only if nonNULL, and returnsTRUE even without a callback.
limits: Search is bounded to the files listed in absence_searches, not the whole repository/binary/ROM. Missing AR9888-specific subtree prevents claiming exhaustive exact-target absence.
Parser-level TRUE is not hardware completion, command availability or an allowlisted safe command.

limits: Arbitrary host-IQ TX is REFUTED for this request schema, not globally disproven for every hidden interface. The meaning of waveformIndex/reference generation and exact AR9888 backend remain UNKNOWN.

Ancestor dl/wlan/Makefile and dl/Makefile raw requests also return404.

No make, compiler, linker, firmware binary or target was run; reproducible complete build/boot is NOT established.

audited_claims.report_correction: Report sections3.2 and4.2 inaccurately imply that UTF_START stops normal WLAN. It requires OFF and returns EBUSY when active. UTF_STOP ends in OFF; normal WLAN is not restored automatically.

evidence.conclusion: Start requires the OFF state. It rejects an already running UTF instance with EALREADY and an active driver with EBUSY. It powers hardware, starts the core in UTF mode and changes driver state; it does not stop an active WLAN automatically.
Stop shuts down the core and HIF power, frees UTF resources and returns the driver to OFF. It does not restore or start normal WLAN firmware.

audited_claims.conclusion: Raw WMI and segmented TLV transports exist. API1 fallback forces10.1 operation versions, but the segmented path sends literal WMI_PDEV_UTF_CMDID while10x has its own command map. Generic segmentation is not a qualified exact-AR9888 exchange.

evidence.conclusion: The TLV path splits data into 252-byte pieces, adds a TLV and little-endian segment header, and sends the literal WMI_PDEV_UTF_CMDID. Exact target compatibility is not established.
The 10.1 family maps a distinct UTF command enum. The testmode segmented path uses a literal main enum, so equivalence must not be assumed.

audited_claims.conclusion: GET_VERSION queries the host testmode ABI, not target capabilities. Adding DATA changes command zero into TLV transmission. A future version-only allowlist must require DATA to be absent.

evidence.conclusion: Command zero without DATA queries the host testmode ABI. The same command with DATA transmits segmented TLV data. Unknown commands return EOPNOTSUPP.
UTF_START is 1, UTF_STOP is 2 and raw WMI is 3. Segmented TLV aliases GET_VERSION zero and is distinguished by the DATA attribute.

audited_claims.conclusion: The receiver checks minimum header size and the2048-byte accumulation cap. It does not compare current_seq with expected_seq or validate msgref and advertised total length. The5000-byte input policy can require20chunks although the segment count is four bits. No safe payload limit or robust session validation is established. No fuzzing, exploitation or device execution was performed.

evidence.conclusion: Response accumulation is limited to 2048 bytes. The receiver reads current_seq but does not compare it with expected_seq; it does not validate msgref or the advertised total length here.
The TLV path splits data into 252-byte pieces, adds a TLV and little-endian segment header, and sends the literal WMI_PDEV_UTF_CMDID. Exact target compatibility is not established.
The host ABI is 1.0. The DATA attribute permits up to 5000 bytes; accumulated FTM response storage is 2048 bytes.

audited_claims.conclusion: BMI read_memory uses a distinct READ opcode,256-byte chunks, the done_sent EBUSY gate and HIF error propagation. Memory/register writes, execute and download are separate operations. This boot interface is not ordinary runtime firmware access and provides no experiment-specific address or register-side-effect allowlist.

evidence.conclusion: READ_MEMORY uses chunks no larger than 256 bytes. It returns EBUSY after DONE and propagates HIF exchange errors. It is neither a runtime WMI memory API nor an address allowlist.
The documentation explicitly describes a QCA988x boot-only interface. Its 256-byte transfer encoding is not a safety guarantee for arbitrary addresses.

audited_claims.conclusion: The QCA988X hw2 PCI table confirms DRAM at0x400000 with length0x50000, not the whole memory map. RAM dumping requires DEV_COREDUMP, the RAM mask bit, a matching target/hardware/bus tuple, allocated storage and successful diagnostic reads. The default mask omits RAM. Dumps can be partial; crash recovery and CE activity are not passive or proven health-preserving.

evidence.conclusion: The QCA988X hw2 PCI table contains DRAM at 0x400000 with length 0x50000 and register regions at 0x4000 with length 0x2000 and 0x8000 with length 0x58000. This dump table is not a complete silicon memory map.
RAM dumping requires its mask bit and an exact target_version, hardware revision and bus match. No matching layout returns NULL.
The default mask includes register and Copy Engine data only, not RAM. The coredump_mask parameter has mode0444; it is not a writable runtime knob here.
Crash work collects registers, Copy Engine state and memory, then starts recovery. Deliberately crashing firmware is not a passive read and was not performed.

audited_claims.report_refinement: The pinned source refutes an absolute claim that stock ath10k never exports raw RX descriptor bytes. An optional trace event copies the descriptor array, including version1 QCA988X PPDU metadata. One AMSDU path omits its first u32; a monitor AMSDU physical-address path traces the full descriptor. Ordinary SKB payload strips the descriptor and ordinary RX status does not export a full EVM/H matrix.

evidence.conclusion: QCA988X uses sizeof(htt_rx_desc_v1) and its MSDU payload offset. This closes the core-to-operations-to-descriptor-layout source chain.
The RX descriptor prefix is removed from the logical SKB payload, but its retained bytes remain available to this trace call. This AMSDU path traces the descriptor except its first u32.
The monitor AMSDU handler using physical-address indications traces the full descriptor size before pulling the descriptor from the SKB.
The trace entry copies a dynamic raw descriptor byte array. Its text formatter prints only the length; the binary trace entry contains bytes. This is not channel-dump RAM or IQ export.

audited_claims.conclusion: Capture/H-info flags, BB debug length, EVM and timestamps are defined in the QCA988X host descriptor. Trace definitions do not prove firmware populates them, appended H data reaches the host, or channel memory address, format, CSI/IQ streaming and ADC capture are known. Existing descriptor tracing is a simpler export lead to assess before new instrumentation.

evidence.conclusion: The QCA988X layout defines sixteen EVM pilot words, TSF and WB timestamps, an H-info flag, capture bit25 and a BB debug length. Metadata definitions do not prove actual records are delivered.
The documentation describes H information in packet data and channel-dump memory readable by firmware. It supplies no validated buffer address, complex-data format or ADC sample rate.

audited_claims.conclusion: Conditional debugfs mem_value supports reads and writes, mode0600, ON/UTF state and mutex guards. The PCI reader uses CE/DMA with timeouts and completion checks; it still changes transport state and provides no experimental address allowlist. Source API presence is not installed-target availability.

evidence.conclusion: The debugfs reader checks a nonnegative offset, allocation, conf_mutex and ON or UTF state before calling HIF read. It is not an address allowlist or an atomic-snapshot guarantee.
The same debugfs file also supports writes. It must not be classified as read-only merely because a read handler exists.
The reader uses target-to-host Copy Engine DMA in bounded chunks. A mutex serializes access; completion timeouts, sizes and buffer addresses are checked. A read still programs CE/DMA state.
